EDITORIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Agreement is made on 11 January 2026 between Meridian Learning Limited, a company registered in Scotland, whose registered office is at 44 Bellfield Row, Edinburgh EH3 7PT (the "Client"), and Tomas Beck, trading as Beck Editorial, of 2 Wester Lane, Glasgow G12 8QN (the "Contractor").

The parties agree as follows.

1. THE ENGAGEMENT

1.1 The Contractor shall copy-edit and proofread the six online course modules listed in Schedule 1 (the "Deliverables").
1.2 The Contractor shall begin work on 19 January 2026 and shall deliver the last of the Deliverables by 29 May 2026 (the "Term").
1.3 Each party shall give the other the information and access it reasonably needs to perform this Agreement.
1.4 This Agreement does not renew, and any further engagement of the Contractor requires a fresh written agreement signed by both parties.

2. HOW THE WORK IS DELIVERED

2.1 The Contractor shall deliver each Deliverable to the Client by the date shown against it in Schedule 1.
2.2 The Contractor shall deliver each Deliverable as an edited manuscript with tracked changes and a short note listing the editorial decisions taken.
2.3 The Contractor shall carry out one round of revisions to each Deliverable at no additional charge, to be requested by the Client in writing within the acceptance period in clause 4.2.

3. CHANGES

3.1 A change to the Deliverables, to the Term or to the fee takes effect only once both parties have signed a written change order recording it.
3.2 Neither party may vary the fee, the scope of the Deliverables or the delivery dates without the other party's written agreement.

4. FEES, ACCEPTANCE AND PAYMENT

4.1 The Client shall pay the Contractor £480 for each module edited under this Agreement, invoiced on acceptance of that module.
4.2 The Client shall notify the Contractor in writing within ten (10) working days of delivery whether a Deliverable meets the acceptance criteria in Schedule 2, identifying by reference to those criteria anything that does not.
4.3 A Deliverable is treated as accepted if the Client gives no notice under clause 4.2 within that period.
4.4 Where the Client gives notice that a Deliverable does not meet the acceptance criteria, the Contractor shall correct the items identified within ten (10) working days and the Deliverable is then reassessed against the same criteria.
4.5 The Client shall pay each invoice within fourteen (14) days of the date of the invoice.
4.6 Interest accrues on any sum not paid when due at four per cent (4%) a year above the Bank of England base rate, from the due date until payment.

5. CONFIDENTIALITY

5.1 Each party shall keep confidential the other party's commercial, technical and learner information disclosed to it under this Agreement, and shall use that information only for the purposes of this Agreement.
5.2 Clause 5.1 does not apply to information that is already public, that becomes public otherwise than through a breach of this Agreement, or that a party is required by law to disclose.

6. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

6.1 On payment in full for a Deliverable, the Contractor assigns to the Client the copyright and all other intellectual property rights in that Deliverable.
6.2 The Contractor's pre-existing materials, including its style guides, editing macros and house templates, remain the Contractor's property, and the Contractor grants the Client a perpetual, non-exclusive licence to use them so far as they are embedded in a Deliverable.
6.3 Neither party acquires any right in the other party's trade marks or brand assets under this Agreement.

7. STATUS OF THE CONTRACTOR

7.1 The Contractor is an independent contractor and nothing in this Agreement makes the Contractor an employee, agent or partner of the Client.
7.2 The Contractor decides how and when to carry out the work, subject only to the delivery dates in Schedule 1.

8. INDEMNITY AND LIABILITY

8.1 Each party shall indemnify the other against any claim brought by a third party to the extent that the claim arises from that party's own breach of this Agreement.
8.2 The total liability of each party under this Agreement, whether in contract, delict or otherwise, is limited to the total fees payable under clause 4.
8.3 Nothing in this Agreement limits either party's liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, or for fraud.

9. ENDING THIS AGREEMENT

9.1 Either party may end this Agreement by giving the other thirty (30) days' written notice.
9.2 Where the Client ends this Agreement under clause 9.1, the Client shall pay for every Deliverable accepted or delivered before the end date, for work in progress on the date of the notice, and a cancellation fee of twenty-five per cent (25%) of the fees for the modules not yet started.
9.3 Where the Contractor ends this Agreement under clause 9.1, the Contractor shall deliver the work in progress and shall repay any part of the fee paid for work not performed.
9.4 Clauses 5, 6 and 8 survive the end of this Agreement.

10. AFTER THE TERM

10.1 Neither party restricts the other from working with any client, customer or supplier after the end of this Agreement.

11. NOTICES

11.1 A notice under this Agreement must be in writing and sent to the address shown at the head of this Agreement or to an email address the receiving party has given for the purpose.

12. GOVERNING LAW

12.1 This Agreement and any dispute arising out of or in connection with it are governed by the law of Scotland, and the parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Scottish courts.

13. WHOLE AGREEMENT

13.1 This Agreement is the whole agreement between the parties about the Deliverables and replaces any earlier proposal, quotation or discussion.

SCHEDULE 1 — THE DELIVERABLES

Module 1: Getting started with data, due 6 February 2026.
Module 2: Working with spreadsheets, due 27 February 2026.
Module 3: Cleaning a dataset, due 20 March 2026.
Module 4: Charts that answer a question, due 17 April 2026.
Module 5: Sharing an analysis, due 8 May 2026.
Module 6: Course review and glossary, due 29 May 2026.

SCHEDULE 2 — ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

A Deliverable meets the acceptance criteria when all five of the following are true.
Criterion 1: Every sentence conforms to the Client's published style guide, a copy of which is attached to this Agreement.
Criterion 2: No spelling, grammar or punctuation error remains, tested against the style guide's British English convention.
Criterion 3: Every heading level follows the module template supplied by the Client.
Criterion 4: Every external link resolves and points at the source named in the text.
Criterion 5: The editorial note required by clause 2.2 lists each substantive change and the reason for it.

Signed for and on behalf of Meridian Learning Limited.

Signed by Tomas Beck, trading as Beck Editorial.
